EFW_Mero.name: General Mero
EFW_Mero.role: A commanding figure from the forgotten war whose memory begins bleeding through Theo
EFW_Mero.notes: Mero is not a hologram, AI tutor or technical interface. He appears as remembered authority: posture, voice, expectation, habit and moral pressure. Whether Theo is remembering Mero, remembering serving Mero, or being remembered by Mero remains unresolved in Episode 2. Mero speaks in decisions, obligations, sacrifice and command—not calculations.

EFW_Kyn.name: Kyn
EFW_Kyn.role: Relay-station colleague who becomes Rae's grounded human counterweight
EFW_Kyn.notes: Practical and personally attentive. Kyn cares whether Rae survives and is increasingly frustrated by her tendency to hide fear inside analysis. He speaks plainly and forces Rae back toward people rather than abstractions.

EFW_Korsen.name: Korsen
EFW_Korsen.notes: Disciplined, cautious and suspicious. He does not trade engineering jargon with Theo; he wants the forbidden object surrendered and his people kept alive.

EFW_Tallis.name: Tallis
EFW_Tallis.role: Nuxis Array archivist guarding sealed records
EFW_Tallis.notes: A frightened but principled archivist caught between institutional oath and Adrian. His resistance matters because Adrian's coercion of him marks Adrian's erosion of neutrality.

EFW_Tarn.name: Tarn
EFW_Tarn.role: Municipal officer blocking Theo's escape through the cargo bay
EFW_Tarn.notes: A working officer rather than a faceless tactical calculator. He sees Theo briefly become someone older and more authoritative than the junior attaché in front of him.

EFW_Vorn.name: Vorn
EFW_Vorn.role: Municipal enforcer who corners Theo in the main transit junction
EFW_Vorn.notes: Alert and increasingly unsettled by Theo's changing manner. He is the first present-day adversary to ask, in effect, who Theo has become.

EFW_Archivist.name: Nuxis Archivist
EFW_Archivist.role: Archive clerk pressured by Adrian during the Nuxis breach
EFW_Archivist.notes: Ordinary institutional worker used to expose how far Adrian is willing to go. Keep the clerk human and frightened; do not reduce the scene to access-protocol mechanics.
